native_mcp_support.notes: Remote MCP servers are a first-class tool type on the Responses API (server_url / connector_id / tunnel_id, allowed_tools, defer_loading, allowed_callers, require_approval) and every current GPT-5.4/5.5/5.6 model page lists 'MCP: Supported'. Re-verified 2026-08-19.

skills_concept.value: Skills (Responses API / Codex): versioned bundles of files plus a SKILL.md manifest, compatible with the open Agent Skills standard, loaded progressively — name/description/path stub always in context, full instructions read on invocation. GPTs/Assistants remain the ChatGPT-product analog; the Agents SDK is the orchestration layer.
skills_concept.notes: Re-verified 2026-08-19. Documented ingest caps: 50 MB zip, 500 files per version, 25 MB per uncompressed file. Skill instructions are billed as USER prompt input, not system input.

release_date.notes: GA date. The API changelog dates the GPT-5.6 family release to July 9, 2026; the launch post (https://openai.com/index/gpt-5-6/) describes a same-day rollout 'gradually toward full availability over the next 24 hours'. Preview announced 2026-06-26 (https://openai.com/index/previewing-gpt-5-6-sol/).

knowledge_cutoff.notes: February 16, 2026 — a ~2.5-month advance over gpt-5.5 (2025-12-01) and ~5.5 months over the gpt-5.4 family (2025-08-31).

context_window_tokens.notes: 1,050,000 tokens, unchanged from gpt-5.5/gpt-5.4. Prompts over 272K input tokens are billed at 2x input / 1.5x output for the whole request.

input_output_shared.notes: Single 1,050,000-token pool shared by input and output.

max_input_tokens.notes: Derived: 1,050,000 - 128,000 = 922,000. Not published as a separate figure.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: No default max_output published; the model page states only the 128,000 maximum.

extended_context.notes: 1,050,000 is the GA window; no beta/extended mode documented. The >272K threshold is a pricing boundary, not a second window.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: reasoning_effort on the GPT-5.6 family: none, low, medium (default), high, xhigh and 'max' — 'max' is new in this generation (gpt-5.5/5.4 stop at xhigh). Reasoning tokens appear in completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens and bill as output, so raising effort raises cost on the expensive side of the ledger.

tokenizer_family.notes: tiktoken's model.py maps the GPT-5 family to o200k_base via MODEL_TO_ENCODING ('gpt-5') and the 'gpt-5-' prefix entry in MODEL_PREFIX_TO_ENCODING; no encoding newer than o200k_base exists for the hosted GPT-5.x models (o200k_harmony is the open-weight gpt-oss variant). Source changed from a tiktoken issue thread to the mapping file itself.

tokenizer_public.notes: tiktoken is open source (MIT) on GitHub and PyPI, so GPT-5.x token counts are reproducible offline — unusual among frontier vendors.

tokenizer_access.notes: pip install tiktoken; encodings o200k_base and cl100k_base ship with the package.

count_tokens_method.value: Server-side (exact, includes tools): POST /v1/responses/input_tokens with the same payload you would send to responses.create. Offline estimate: import tiktoken; enc = tiktoken.get_encoding('o200k_base'); len(enc.encode(text)).
count_tokens_method.notes: CHANGED: the token-counting guide now documents a dedicated endpoint, POST /v1/responses/input_tokens, which accepts text, messages, images, files, tools and conversations and returns an exact count — the correct way to measure an MCP server's startup footprint, since local tiktoken cannot reproduce the hidden tool/skill scaffolding or image patching. Previous entry cited include=['usage'] round-trips instead.

image_token_rule.value: Patch-based (32x32 pixel patches). Detail levels low, high, original, auto; on GPT-5.6 auto and the omitted default are equivalent to 'original', and with original/auto no patch or dimension ceiling is documented — images are accepted at native resolution. Token cost = resized patch count x a model-specific multiplier. Image input only.
image_token_rule.notes: New in GPT-5.6 (changelog 2026-07-09): images are accepted at original dimensions under original/auto detail, and since auto is also the default, the vision guide warns 'large images can use more input tokens than they did with earlier models'. Unlike gpt-5.5/5.4 no 2,500/10,000-patch ceiling is documented to bound the count, so an unconstrained image can consume a large and unpredictable share of the window; what still binds is the 512 MB / 1,500-image request ceiling and the 1,050,000-token context window — set detail=high or low deliberately. Request ceilings: under 512 MB image payload and up to 1,500 images per request. Multiplier unpublished; use POST /v1/responses/input_tokens for exact counts.

audio_token_rule.notes: Model page lists Audio: not supported (text and image input, text output only). Audio work goes to the gpt-realtime / gpt-transcribe families, which are separate models and out of scope for this entry.

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: Source corrected on 2026-08-19: the previously cited tiktoken cookbook does not in fact state a ratio. OpenAI's help article does: '1 token ~ 4 characters' and '1 token ~ 3/4 of a word' for English. Rule of thumb only — JSON tool definitions tokenize denser than prose, so use the input_tokens endpoint for footprint numbers.

native_mcp.notes: Model page lists 'MCP: Supported'. Remote MCP servers attach as a first-class tool type on the Responses API (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp).

parallel_tool_calls.notes: The function-calling guide documents parallel_tool_calls and states that setting it to false 'ensures exactly zero or one tool is called'; default behaviour allows multiple tool calls in one turn.

max_tools_hard.notes: AGGREGATE scope (all connected MCP servers + built-in/hosted tools in one request's tools array). NO CURRENT TIER-1 PAGE STATES A NUMERIC CAP, so the value is null. Pages opened 2026-08-19: the function-calling guide (this source_url) states no maximum and instead says 'Aim for fewer than 20 functions available at the start of a turn at any one time, though this is just a soft suggestion'; the Responses API reference (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/api-reference/responses/create) documents no maxItems on the tools array; the Chat Completions reference (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/api-reference/chat/create) documents no count limit; the tool-search guide (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-tool-search) gives only a 'fewer than 10 functions' per-namespace best practice. REMOVED the previous value of 128: it was cited to the Assistants API deep-dive ('give the Assistant access to up to 128 tools'), which is a per-Assistant cap on a different, dying surface -- that page carries the banner 'we've deprecated the Assistants API. It will shut down on August 26, 2026' -- so it is not evidence for the GPT-5.x Responses/Chat Completions tools array. What actually binds instead: (1) the context window -- tool definitions are serialized into the request and billed as input tokens (see tool_defs_count_as_input); (2) OpenAI's own <20-functions-at-turn-start guidance, recorded in max_tools_practical; (3) tool search / deferred loading, which moves rarely-used tools out of the up-front array. Tier-4 practitioner reports still quote the rejection "Invalid 'tools': array too long. Expected an array with maximum length 128" on Chat Completions (https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/2848, 2026-03-26; https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/42393); that is an observed error message, not published spec, and no vendor page confirms it for the GPT-5.6 family, so it is not recorded as a value.

max_tools_practical.notes: EMPIRICAL / soft guidance, not a spec cap. Changed from 40 (2026-06-21) because OpenAI now publishes its own number: 'Aim for fewer than 20 functions available at the start of a turn at any one time, though this is just a soft suggestion.' The tool-search guide adds 'aim to keep each namespace to fewer than 10 functions for better token efficiency and model performance' (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-tool-search). Consistent with the long-standing tier-4 community/Berkeley-FCL observation that tool-selection accuracy starts degrading somewhere in the 30-50 tool range. Confidence medium: it is vendor advice about behaviour, not an enforced limit.

tool_definition_shape.notes: OpenAI function/tool JSON: {type:'function', name, description, parameters, strict}. The guide states functions 'are injected into the system message in a syntax the model has been trained on', so shape directly determines the token count.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Token-counting guide, verbatim: 'Tool definitions (function schemas, MCP servers, etc.) add tokens to the context. Count them together with your input.' The function-calling guide adds that function definitions 'count against the model's context limit and are billed as input tokens.'

tool_search_deferral.notes: Model page lists 'Tool search: Supported'. Tool search plus the MCP tool's defer_loading is OpenAI's documented answer to a tool surface larger than a model can usefully hold up front: definitions are discovered at runtime and the cached prefix is preserved when new tools appear. Recommended granularity is namespaces or whole MCP servers rather than individual deferred functions, keeping each namespace under ~10 functions.

max_tool_name_len.notes: CHANGED from 64 (2026-06-21). The Responses API reference now documents the function tool's `name` as minLength 1 / maxLength 128. The previously cited 64-character cap could no longer be found on any currently-reachable OpenAI page — the function-calling guide (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling) no longer states a name length or pattern at all. Confidence medium because the older 64-char Chat-Completions figure is still widely repeated downstream and the two surfaces may differ. Practical impact is unchanged: MCP clients namespace tool names ('<server>_<tool>'), and that prefix is spent from this budget.

max_tool_description_len.notes: Confidence downgraded medium -> low on 2026-08-19. Still undocumented on any OpenAI page: the Responses and Chat references say the description 'has a maximum length' without printing the number. The only public evidence remains the API error text "Invalid 'tools[1].function.description': string too long. Expected a string with maximum length 1024" reported in the linked thread (2024-09-22, last activity 2025-03-27). Not re-confirmed against GPT-5.6 in this pass. Mitigation is unchanged: move long guidance out of the tool description and into the system prompt or a skill.

max_request_size.notes: NUMERIC + NARROW SCOPE (fixed 2026-08-19; was the malformed string '512MB' with unit 'bytes'). The only per-request byte ceiling OpenAI publishes is on the images/vision guide, verbatim 'Up to 512 MB total payload size per request' alongside 'Up to 1500 individual image inputs per request' -- i.e. it is documented for requests carrying image inputs, not as a general JSON body limit. No general request-body byte cap is documented for Chat Completions or the Responses API (checked the API references and the rate-limits guide on 2026-08-19). Do NOT read this as directly comparable to Anthropic's 32 MB or Gemini's 100 MB general request ceilings. For MCP work the binding ceiling is the token side: tool definitions and tool results are input tokens against the context window, not bytes.

max_tool_result_size.notes: EMPIRICAL, not spec (tier 4, low confidence). Value made numeric 2026-08-19 (was the string '512KB'). Re-opened the cited OpenAI developer-forum thread: it reports a 512KB ceiling on submitted tool output, and its own respondent states "I can't find anywhere within the documentation that states this limit exists" -- still undocumented on any OpenAI page, and not re-confirmed against the GPT-5.6 Responses API. Independently, tool RESULTS are ordinary input tokens on the next turn, so a chatty tool consumes the context window regardless of any byte cap; Programmatic Tool Calling is OpenAI's documented mitigation because the program can filter intermediate results before they reach the model.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: No per-request numeric cap on how many tool calls the model may emit in one turn is documented; parallel_tool_calls is a boolean, and the only documented setting is false, which forces exactly zero or one call. What does bind: the size of the aggregate tools array (no vendor-published numeric cap -- see max_tools_hard), the context window that every call and result is charged against, and the per-tier MCP tool-call rate limits (200/1000/2000 RPM).

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No API-enforced cap on tool-call/result cycles per turn is documented; the agents guide describes the loop as SDK-provided and application-managed ('SDK sessions', 'Conversations API', manual history, resumable run state) and prints no numeric ceiling. What bounds a run in practice: the context window, the cost/rate limits, and whatever max-turns guard the calling SDK sets.

max_connected_servers.notes: No numeric cap on connected MCP servers is documented for either the Responses API or ChatGPT. The ChatGPT help article confirms a workspace 'can invoke multiple first-party and third-party apps in a single prompt' without printing a ceiling. The limits that actually bind are aggregate: the size of the tools array summed over all servers (no vendor-published numeric cap -- see max_tools_hard), and the context window those definitions are charged to.

max_total_tools.notes: AGGREGATE ceiling across every connected MCP server plus built-in tools, in one request. Null for the same reason as max_tools_hard: no current OpenAI page publishes a numeric ceiling on the tools array. Verified 2026-08-19 against the function-calling guide (this source_url), the Responses API reference (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/api-reference/responses/create -- no maxItems on tools), the Chat Completions reference and the tool-search guide (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-tool-search). The previously recorded 128 came from the Assistants API deep-dive, a per-Assistant cap on an API that shuts down 2026-08-26, and has been withdrawn. Budget allocation is therefore governed by the context window (tool definitions are input tokens), OpenAI's 'fewer than 20 functions at the start of a turn' guidance, and the per-namespace 'fewer than 10 functions' advice for deferred tools; no vendor page publishes a ceiling on how many tools may be registered behind tool search.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Function/tool `parameters` use OpenAI's Structured Outputs JSON Schema subset. Strict mode (strict:true) requires additionalProperties:false on every object and every property listed in 'required'; the root object may not be anyOf; anyOf members must themselves stay in the subset. Unsupported (silently dropped / rejected) keywords per Microsoft Foundry's Azure OpenAI mirror of this page (last updated 2026-08-06, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/structured-outputs): string minLength/maxLength/pattern/format; number minimum/maximum/multipleOf; object patternProperties/unevaluatedProperties/propertyNames/minProperties/maxProperties; array unevaluatedItems/contains/minContains/maxContains/minItems/maxItems/uniqueItems. SIZE-LIMIT CONFLICT (recorded, unresolved): the Azure mirror still states '100 object properties total' and '5 levels of nesting', while OpenAI announced raised limits on 2025-07-11 (5,000 properties, 120,000 characters per string, 1,000 enum values, 15,000 total chars across enum members when >250 values) as relayed at https://community.openai.com/t/structured-outputs-limits-are-raised-to-support-larger-schemas/1313593 (tier 3, community relay of an @OpenAIDevs post). OpenAI's own current Structured Outputs page (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs) links to a 'supported schemas' detail page that no longer resolves, so no tier-1 OpenAI page currently states either set of numbers. Treat 100 properties / 5 levels as the conservative floor and 5,000 / 10 as unconfirmed. No documented byte-size cap on the serialized tool-definition payload beyond the context window itself.
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: Remote MCP (Responses API, https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp): a server is attached with server_url / connector_id / tunnel_id; its tool definitions are fetched at request time and billed as input tokens ('we charge for tokens used when importing tool definitions or making tool calls. There are no additional fees involved per tool call'). No per-server or per-request cap on the NUMBER of MCP servers is documented — the binding ceiling is the aggregate size of the tools array (no vendor-published numeric cap -- see max_tools_hard) plus the context window. allowed_tools filters which of a server's tools are exposed; defer_loading hands discovery to tool search; allowed_callers ['direct','programmatic'] gates whether a tool is reachable from Programmatic Tool Calling; require_approval ('always' default / 'never' / per-tool_names filter) gates writes. MCP tool-call rate limits: 200 RPM (tier 1), 1000 RPM (tiers 2-3), 2000 RPM (tiers 4-5). Programmatic Tool Calling (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling) lets the model emit JavaScript that runs in an isolated V8 runtime and orchestrates tools, which 'can reduce the amount of intermediate tool output added to model context'; no numeric limits on tools, result size or runtime are published, and a running program cannot itself invoke tool search. ChatGPT-product MCP (https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461-developer-mode-apps-and-full-mcp-connectors-in-chatgpt-beta): full MCP with write actions is in beta for Business/Enterprise/Edu; Pro is read/fetch only; multiple first- and third-party apps may be invoked in one prompt with no published app-count cap. Per-model RPM/TPM rate limits apply and are listed on each model page. Programmatic Tool Calling is listed as supported on this model's page.

strict_function_schema.notes: Structured Outputs strict mode applies to function/tool parameters: additionalProperties:false everywhere, all properties required, root may not be anyOf, and a documented list of unsupported keywords. See tool_schema_limits_notes for the unresolved 100-vs-5,000 property-count conflict.

skills_loading_model.notes: Progressive disclosure, not always-on injection: a skill is 'a versioned bundle of files plus a SKILL.md manifest', and the platform adds only each skill's name, description and path to prompt context; the model reads the full SKILL.md only when it decides to invoke the skill.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: Two-stage cost. Stage 1 (always paid, per request): the name + description + path stub for every attached skill. Stage 2 (paid only on invocation): the full SKILL.md body, and any bundled files the model reads. Docs are explicit that 'Skill instructions are user prompt input (not system prompt input), so they're handled with the same priority as other user-provided instructions' — which also means they are ordinary input tokens. Ingest caps documented 2026-08-19: 50 MB max zip upload, 500 max files per skill version, 25 MB max uncompressed file. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-skills.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: The Responses API prepends hidden scaffolding for every enabled surface (MCP server tool lists, skill stubs, hosted-tool definitions). OpenAI does not publish its token size. Measure it empirically by POSTing the same payload with and without each tool to /v1/responses/input_tokens (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/token-counting) and differencing.

prompt_caching.notes: CHANGED CACHE MODEL for GPT-5.6 and later: 1,024 tokens is a strict minimum; default retention is 30 minutes with an explicit TTL via prompt_cache_options.ttl (replacing the 5-10 minute in-memory / 24-hour extended split used by gpt-5.5 and earlier); cached input bills at 0.1x uncached; and cache WRITES now bill at 1.25x the uncached input rate, a surcharge earlier models did not have. For MCP this matters directly: 'tool definitions, tool ordering, and structured output schemas contribute to the prompt prefix', so a server that reorders or edits its tools forces a re-write at 1.25x.

memory_feature.notes: No model-side persistent memory in the API. The agents guide frames state as application-managed — SDK sessions, the Conversations API, manual history, or resumable run state. ChatGPT's 'Memory' and Codex's memories are product features, not this model's API surface.

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Standard processing, prompts under 272K input tokens. Sol launched at $5/$30 and was not part of the 2026-07-30 price cut (which reduced Luna 80% and Terra 20%).

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Standard processing. Prompts over 272K input tokens bill output at 1.5x for the whole request. Reasoning tokens bill at this rate.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: 0.1x the uncached input rate. Note the offsetting 1.25x cache-WRITE charge that is new in the GPT-5.6 generation.

batch_discount.notes: Batch API: 24-hour async processing at 50% off input and output.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Image input billed as ordinary input tokens via 32x32 patch counting. Because auto/original is the GPT-5.6 default and no patch ceiling is documented for it, image cost is not bounded by a published per-image number — the binding ceilings are the 512 MB / 1,500-image request limit and the context window. Pin detail explicitly for predictable billing. Audio is not supported on this model. Speed tiers add multipliers: Fast mode is ~2.5x faster at 2x the price (changelog 2026-07-30, extended to >272K prompts 2026-08-05), and Ultrafast mode for GPT-5.6 Sol (~14x faster) entered limited preview 2026-08-13.

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens is part of completion_tokens. The new 'max' reasoning effort is therefore the most expensive knob on this model.

models.notes: NEW in this refresh. Frontier model of the GPT-5.6 family and OpenAI's current flagship; the bare alias `gpt-5.6` routes to it. Previewed 2026-06-26, GA 2026-07-09. It is the named replacement for gpt-5-2025-08-07, gpt-5-pro-2025-10-06 (with reasoning.mode: pro), gpt-5-chat-latest, gpt-5-codex, gpt-5.1-chat-latest, gpt-5.1-codex, gpt-5.1-codex-max, gpt-5.2-codex, gpt-5.2-chat-latest and gpt-5.3-chat-latest on the deprecations page. MCP-relevant deltas vs gpt-5.5: Programmatic Tool Calling (model-authored JavaScript orchestrating tools in an isolated V8 runtime, with allowed_callers gating on the MCP tool), multi-agent orchestration in beta on the Responses API, a new 'max' reasoning effort, a 30-minute TTL-controlled prompt cache with a 1.25x cache-write charge, and uncapped native-resolution image input by default. Tool limits are unchanged: OpenAI publishes no numeric cap on the tools array (see tools_mcp.max_tools_hard); the context window and the <20-functions-at-turn-start guidance bind. Rate limits at tier 5: 15,000 RPM / 40M TPM.

Changed from 40 (2026-06-21) because OpenAI now publishes its own number: 'Aim for fewer than 20 functions available at the start of a turn at any one time, though this is just a soft suggestion.' Consistent with the long-standing tier-4 community/Berkeley-FCL observation that tool-selection accuracy starts degrading somewhere in the 30-50 tool range. Confidence medium: it is vendor advice about behaviour, not an enforced limit.

tool_definition_shape.notes: OpenAI function/tool JSON: {type:'function', name, description, parameters, strict}. The guide states functions 'are injected into the system message in a syntax the model has been trained on', so shape directly determines the token count.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Token-counting guide, verbatim: 'Tool definitions (function schemas, MCP servers, etc.) add tokens to the context. Count them together with your input.' The function-calling guide adds that function definitions 'count against the model's context limit and are billed as input tokens.'

tool_search_deferral.notes: Model page lists 'Tool search: Supported'. Tool search plus the MCP tool's defer_loading is OpenAI's documented answer to a tool surface larger than a model can usefully hold up front: definitions are discovered at runtime and the cached prefix is preserved when new tools appear. Recommended granularity is namespaces or whole MCP servers rather than individual deferred functions, keeping each namespace under ~10 functions.

max_tool_name_len.notes: CHANGED from 64 (2026-06-21). The Responses API reference now documents the function tool's `name` as minLength 1 / maxLength 128. The previously cited 64-character cap could no longer be found on any currently-reachable OpenAI page — the function-calling guide (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling) no longer states a name length or pattern at all. Confidence medium because the older 64-char Chat-Completions figure is still widely repeated downstream and the two surfaces may differ. Practical impact is unchanged: MCP clients namespace tool names ('<server>_<tool>'), and that prefix is spent from this budget.

max_tool_description_len.notes: Confidence downgraded medium -> low on 2026-08-19. Still undocumented on any OpenAI page: the Responses and Chat references say the description 'has a maximum length' without printing the number. The only public evidence remains the API error text "Invalid 'tools[1].function.description': string too long. Expected a string with maximum length 1024" reported in the linked thread (2024-09-22, last activity 2025-03-27). Not re-confirmed against GPT-5.6 in this pass. Mitigation is unchanged: move long guidance out of the tool description and into the system prompt or a skill.

max_request_size.notes: NUMERIC + NARROW SCOPE (fixed 2026-08-19; was the malformed string '512MB' with unit 'bytes'). The only per-request byte ceiling OpenAI publishes is on the images/vision guide, verbatim 'Up to 512 MB total payload size per request' alongside 'Up to 1500 individual image inputs per request' -- i.e. it is documented for requests carrying image inputs, not as a general JSON body limit. Do NOT read this as directly comparable to Anthropic's 32 MB or Gemini's 100 MB general request ceilings. For MCP work the binding ceiling is the token side: tool definitions and tool results are input tokens against the context window, not bytes.

max_tool_result_size.notes: EMPIRICAL, not spec (tier 4, low confidence). Value made numeric 2026-08-19 (was the string '512KB'). Re-opened the cited OpenAI developer-forum thread: it reports a 512KB ceiling on submitted tool output, and its own respondent states "I can't find anywhere within the documentation that states this limit exists" -- still undocumented on any OpenAI page, and not re-confirmed against the GPT-5.6 Responses API. tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No API-enforced cap on tool-call/result cycles per turn is documented; the agents guide describes the loop as SDK-provided and application-managed ('SDK sessions', 'Conversations API', manual history, resumable run state) and prints no numeric ceiling. What bounds a run in practice: the context window, the cost/rate limits, and whatever max-turns guard the calling SDK sets.

tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: Remote MCP (Responses API, https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp): a server is attached with server_url / connector_id / tunnel_id; its tool definitions are fetched at request time and billed as input tokens ('we charge for tokens used when importing tool definitions or making tool calls. strict_function_schema.notes: Structured Outputs strict mode applies to function/tool parameters: additionalProperties:false everywhere, all properties required, root may not be anyOf, and a documented list of unsupported keywords. skills_loading_model.notes: Progressive disclosure, not always-on injection: a skill is 'a versioned bundle of files plus a SKILL.md manifest', and the platform adds only each skill's name, description and path to prompt context; the model reads the full SKILL.md only when it decides to invoke the skill.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: Two-stage cost. Stage 1 (always paid, per request): the name + description + path stub for every attached skill. Stage 2 (paid only on invocation): the full SKILL.md body, and any bundled files the model reads. Docs are explicit that 'Skill instructions are user prompt input (not system prompt input), so they're handled with the same priority as other user-provided instructions' — which also means they are ordinary input tokens. Ingest caps documented 2026-08-19: 50 MB max zip upload, 500 max files per skill version, 25 MB max uncompressed file. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-skills.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: The Responses API prepends hidden scaffolding for every enabled surface (MCP server tool lists, skill stubs, hosted-tool definitions). OpenAI does not publish its token size. prompt_caching.notes: CHANGED CACHE MODEL for GPT-5.6 and later: 1,024 tokens is a strict minimum; default retention is 30 minutes with an explicit TTL via prompt_cache_options.ttl (replacing the 5-10 minute in-memory / 24-hour extended split used by gpt-5.5 and earlier); cached input bills at 0.1x uncached; and cache WRITES now bill at 1.25x the uncached input rate, a surcharge earlier models did not have. For MCP this matters directly: 'tool definitions, tool ordering, and structured output schemas contribute to the prompt prefix', so a server that reorders or edits its tools forces a re-write at 1.25x.

memory_feature.notes: No model-side persistent memory in the API. The agents guide frames state as application-managed — SDK sessions, the Conversations API, manual history, or resumable run state. ChatGPT's 'Memory' and Codex's memories are product features, not this model's API surface.

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Standard processing, prompts under 272K input tokens. Price CHANGED since the 2026-06-21 snapshot's generation: Terra launched 2026-07-09 at $2.50 input / $15 output and was cut ~20% on 2026-07-30 to the current $2.00 / $12.00 (changelog).

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Standard processing. Prompts over 272K input tokens bill output at 1.5x for the whole request. Reasoning tokens bill at this rate.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: 0.1x the uncached input rate. Note the offsetting 1.25x cache-WRITE charge that is new in the GPT-5.6 generation.

batch_discount.notes: Batch API: 24-hour async processing at 50% off input and output.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Image input billed as ordinary input tokens via 32x32 patch counting. Because auto/original is the GPT-5.6 default and no patch ceiling is documented for it, image cost is not bounded by a published per-image number — the binding ceilings are the 512 MB / 1,500-image request limit and the context window. Pin detail explicitly for predictable billing. Audio is not supported on this model. Speed tiers add multipliers: Fast mode is ~2.5x faster at 2x the price (changelog 2026-07-30, extended to >272K prompts 2026-08-05), and Ultrafast mode for GPT-5.6 Sol (~14x faster) entered limited preview 2026-08-13.

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens is part of completion_tokens. The new 'max' reasoning effort is therefore the most expensive knob on this model.

models.notes: NEW in this refresh. Mid tier of the GPT-5.6 family — 'balances intelligence and cost', the successor slot to the older mini models, and the named replacement for gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07 and gpt-5.1-codex-mini on the deprecations page. GA 2026-07-09. Unlike the previous generation's mini (gpt-5.4-mini, 400K), Terra carries the full 1,050,000-token window, which materially changes MCP planning: a heavy tool surface no longer forces you up to the flagship. Same feature table as Sol including MCP, tool search, skills, Programmatic Tool Calling, computer use and hosted shell. Same aggregate tools-array behaviour, with no vendor-published numeric cap (see tools_mcp.max_tools_hard).

release_date.notes: GA date. The API changelog dates the GPT-5.6 family release to July 9, 2026; the launch post (https://openai.com/index/gpt-5-6/) describes a same-day rollout 'gradually toward full availability over the next 24 hours'. Preview announced 2026-06-26 (https://openai.com/index/previewing-gpt-5-6-sol/).

knowledge_cutoff.notes: February 16, 2026 — a ~2.5-month advance over gpt-5.5 (2025-12-01) and ~5.5 months over the gpt-5.4 family (2025-08-31).

context_window_tokens.notes: 1,050,000 tokens, unchanged from gpt-5.5/gpt-5.4. Prompts over 272K input tokens are billed at 2x input / 1.5x output for the whole request.

input_output_shared.notes: Single 1,050,000-token pool shared by input and output.

max_input_tokens.notes: Derived: 1,050,000 - 128,000 = 922,000. Not published as a separate figure.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: No default max_output published; the model page states only the 128,000 maximum.

extended_context.notes: 1,050,000 is the GA window; no beta/extended mode documented. The >272K threshold is a pricing boundary, not a second window.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: reasoning_effort on the GPT-5.6 family: none, low, medium (default), high, xhigh and 'max' — 'max' is new in this generation (gpt-5.5/5.4 stop at xhigh). Reasoning tokens appear in completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens and bill as output, so raising effort raises cost on the expensive side of the ledger.

tokenizer_family.notes: tiktoken's model.py maps the GPT-5 family to o200k_base via MODEL_TO_ENCODING ('gpt-5') and the 'gpt-5-' prefix entry in MODEL_PREFIX_TO_ENCODING; no encoding newer than o200k_base exists for the hosted GPT-5.x models (o200k_harmony is the open-weight gpt-oss variant). Source changed from a tiktoken issue thread to the mapping file itself.

tokenizer_public.notes: tiktoken is open source (MIT) on GitHub and PyPI, so GPT-5.x token counts are reproducible offline — unusual among frontier vendors.

tokenizer_access.notes: pip install tiktoken; encodings o200k_base and cl100k_base ship with the package.

count_tokens_method.value: Server-side (exact, includes tools): POST /v1/responses/input_tokens with the same payload you would send to responses.create. Offline estimate: import tiktoken; enc = tiktoken.get_encoding('o200k_base'); len(enc.encode(text)).
count_tokens_method.notes: CHANGED: the token-counting guide now documents a dedicated endpoint, POST /v1/responses/input_tokens, which accepts text, messages, images, files, tools and conversations and returns an exact count — the correct way to measure an MCP server's startup footprint, since local tiktoken cannot reproduce the hidden tool/skill scaffolding or image patching. Previous entry cited include=['usage'] round-trips instead.

image_token_rule.value: Patch-based (32x32 pixel patches). Detail levels low, high, original, auto; on GPT-5.6 auto and the omitted default are equivalent to 'original', and with original/auto no patch or dimension ceiling is documented — images are accepted at native resolution. Token cost = resized patch count x a model-specific multiplier. Image input only.
image_token_rule.notes: New in GPT-5.6 (changelog 2026-07-09): images are accepted at original dimensions under original/auto detail, and since auto is also the default, the vision guide warns 'large images can use more input tokens than they did with earlier models'. Unlike gpt-5.5/5.4 no 2,500/10,000-patch ceiling is documented to bound the count, so an unconstrained image can consume a large and unpredictable share of the window; what still binds is the 512 MB / 1,500-image request ceiling and the 1,050,000-token context window — set detail=high or low deliberately. Request ceilings: under 512 MB image payload and up to 1,500 images per request. Multiplier unpublished; use POST /v1/responses/input_tokens for exact counts.

audio_token_rule.notes: Model page lists Audio: not supported (text and image input, text output only). Audio work goes to the gpt-realtime / gpt-transcribe families, which are separate models and out of scope for this entry.

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: Source corrected on 2026-08-19: the previously cited tiktoken cookbook does not in fact state a ratio. OpenAI's help article does: '1 token ~ 4 characters' and '1 token ~ 3/4 of a word' for English. Rule of thumb only — JSON tool definitions tokenize denser than prose, so use the input_tokens endpoint for footprint numbers.

native_mcp.notes: Model page lists 'MCP: Supported'. Remote MCP servers attach as a first-class tool type on the Responses API (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp).

parallel_tool_calls.notes: The function-calling guide documents parallel_tool_calls and states that setting it to false 'ensures exactly zero or one tool is called'; default behaviour allows multiple tool calls in one turn.

max_tools_hard.notes: AGGREGATE scope (all connected MCP servers + built-in/hosted tools in one request's tools array). NO CURRENT TIER-1 PAGE STATES A NUMERIC CAP, so the value is null. native_mcp.notes: Model page lists 'MCP: Supported'. Remote MCP servers attach as a first-class tool type on the Responses API (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp).

parallel_tool_calls.notes: The function-calling guide documents parallel_tool_calls and states that setting it to false 'ensures exactly zero or one tool is called'; default behaviour allows multiple tool calls in one turn.

max_tools_hard.notes: AGGREGATE scope (all connected MCP servers + built-in/hosted tools in one request's tools array). NO CURRENT TIER-1 PAGE STATES A NUMERIC CAP, so the value is null. Pages opened 2026-08-19: the function-calling guide (this source_url) states no maximum and instead says 'Aim for fewer than 20 functions available at the start of a turn at any one time, though this is just a soft suggestion'; the Responses API reference (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/api-reference/responses/create) documents no maxItems on the tools array; the Chat Completions reference (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/api-reference/chat/create) documents no count limit; the tool-search guide (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-tool-search) gives only a 'fewer than 10 functions' per-namespace best practice. It will shut down on August 26, 2026' -- so it is not evidence for the GPT-5.x Responses/Chat Completions tools array. Tier-4 practitioner reports still quote the rejection "Invalid 'tools': array too long. Expected an array with maximum length 128" on Chat Completions (https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/2848, 2026-03-26; https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/42393); that is an observed error message, not published spec, and no vendor page confirms it for the GPT-5.6 family, so it is not recorded as a value.

max_tools_practical.notes: EMPIRICAL / soft guidance, not a spec cap. The tool-search guide adds 'aim to keep each namespace to fewer than 10 functions for better token efficiency and model performance' (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-tool-search). Consistent with the long-standing tier-4 community/Berkeley-FCL observation that tool-selection accuracy starts degrading somewhere in the 30-50 tool range. Confidence medium: it is vendor advice about behaviour, not an enforced limit.

tool_definition_shape.notes: OpenAI function/tool JSON: {type:'function', name, description, parameters, strict}. The guide states functions 'are injected into the system message in a syntax the model has been trained on', so shape directly determines the token count.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Token-counting guide, verbatim: 'Tool definitions (function schemas, MCP servers, etc.) add tokens to the context. Count them together with your input.' The function-calling guide adds that function definitions 'count against the model's context limit and are billed as input tokens.'

tool_search_deferral.notes: Model page lists 'Tool search: Supported'. gpt-5.4 is the earliest model with tool_search — 'tool search is supported on gpt-5.4 and later models'. Pair with the MCP tool's defer_loading to keep a large server catalog out of the up-front tools array.

max_tool_name_len.notes: CHANGED from 64 (2026-06-21). The Responses API reference now documents the function tool's `name` as minLength 1 / maxLength 128. The previously cited 64-character cap could no longer be found on any currently-reachable OpenAI page — the function-calling guide (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling) no longer states a name length or pattern at all. Confidence medium because the older 64-char Chat-Completions figure is still widely repeated downstream and the two surfaces may differ. Practical impact is unchanged: MCP clients namespace tool names ('<server>_<tool>'), and that prefix is spent from this budget.

max_tool_description_len.notes: Confidence downgraded medium -> low on 2026-08-19. Still undocumented on any OpenAI page: the Responses and Chat references say the description 'has a maximum length' without printing the number. The only public evidence remains the API error text "Invalid 'tools[1].function.description': string too long. Expected a string with maximum length 1024" reported in the linked thread (2024-09-22, last activity 2025-03-27). Not re-confirmed against GPT-5.6 in this pass. Mitigation is unchanged: move long guidance out of the tool description and into the system prompt or a skill.

max_request_size.notes: NUMERIC + NARROW SCOPE (fixed 2026-08-19; was the malformed string '512MB' with unit 'bytes'). The only per-request byte ceiling OpenAI publishes is on the images/vision guide, verbatim 'Up to 512 MB total payload size per request' alongside 'Up to 1500 individual image inputs per request' -- i.e. it is documented for requests carrying image inputs, not as a general JSON body limit. No general request-body byte cap is documented for Chat Completions or the Responses API (checked the API references and the rate-limits guide on 2026-08-19). Do NOT read this as directly comparable to Anthropic's 32 MB or Gemini's 100 MB general request ceilings. For MCP work the binding ceiling is the token side: tool definitions and tool results are input tokens against the context window, not bytes.

max_tool_result_size.notes: EMPIRICAL, not spec (tier 4, low confidence). Value made numeric 2026-08-19 (was the string '512KB'). Re-opened the cited OpenAI developer-forum thread: it reports a 512KB ceiling on submitted tool output, and its own respondent states "I can't find anywhere within the documentation that states this limit exists" -- still undocumented on any OpenAI page, and not re-confirmed against the GPT-5.6 Responses API. Independently, tool RESULTS are ordinary input tokens on the next turn, so a chatty tool consumes the context window regardless of any byte cap; Programmatic Tool Calling is OpenAI's documented mitigation because the program can filter intermediate results before they reach the model.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: No per-request numeric cap on how many tool calls the model may emit in one turn is documented; parallel_tool_calls is a boolean, and the only documented setting is false, which forces exactly zero or one call. What does bind: the size of the aggregate tools array (no vendor-published numeric cap -- see max_tools_hard), the context window that every call and result is charged against, and the per-tier MCP tool-call rate limits (200/1000/2000 RPM).

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No API-enforced cap on tool-call/result cycles per turn is documented; the agents guide describes the loop as SDK-provided and application-managed ('SDK sessions', 'Conversations API', manual history, resumable run state) and prints no numeric ceiling. What bounds a run in practice: the context window, the cost/rate limits, and whatever max-turns guard the calling SDK sets.

max_connected_servers.notes: No numeric cap on connected MCP servers is documented for either the Responses API or ChatGPT. The limits that actually bind are aggregate: the size of the tools array summed over all servers (no vendor-published numeric cap -- see max_tools_hard), and the context window those definitions are charged to.

max_total_tools.notes: AGGREGATE ceiling across every connected MCP server plus built-in tools, in one request. tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Function/tool `parameters` use OpenAI's Structured Outputs JSON Schema subset. Strict mode (strict:true) requires additionalProperties:false on every object and every property listed in 'required'; the root object may not be anyOf; anyOf members must themselves stay in the subset. Unsupported (silently dropped / rejected) keywords per Microsoft Foundry's Azure OpenAI mirror of this page (last updated 2026-08-06, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/structured-outputs): string minLength/maxLength/pattern/format; number minimum/maximum/multipleOf; object patternProperties/unevaluatedProperties/propertyNames/minProperties/maxProperties; array unevaluatedItems/contains/minContains/maxContains/minItems/maxItems/uniqueItems. SIZE-LIMIT CONFLICT (recorded, unresolved): the Azure mirror still states '100 object properties total' and '5 levels of nesting', while OpenAI announced raised limits on 2025-07-11 (5,000 properties, 120,000 characters per string, 1,000 enum values, 15,000 total chars across enum members when >250 values) as relayed at https://community.openai.com/t/structured-outputs-limits-are-raised-to-support-larger-schemas/1313593 (tier 3, community relay of an @OpenAIDevs post). OpenAI's own current Structured Outputs page (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs) links to a 'supported schemas' detail page that no longer resolves, so no tier-1 OpenAI page currently states either set of numbers. Treat 100 properties / 5 levels as the conservative floor and 5,000 / 10 as unconfirmed. No documented byte-size cap on the serialized tool-definition payload beyond the context window itself.
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: Remote MCP (Responses API, https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp): a server is attached with server_url / connector_id / tunnel_id; its tool definitions are fetched at request time and billed as input tokens ('we charge for tokens used when importing tool definitions or making tool calls. There are no additional fees involved per tool call'). No per-server or per-request cap on the NUMBER of MCP servers is documented — the binding ceiling is the aggregate size of the tools array (no vendor-published numeric cap -- see max_tools_hard) plus the context window. allowed_tools filters which of a server's tools are exposed; defer_loading hands discovery to tool search; allowed_callers ['direct','programmatic'] gates whether a tool is reachable from Programmatic Tool Calling; require_approval ('always' default / 'never' / per-tool_names filter) gates writes. MCP tool-call rate limits: 200 RPM (tier 1), 1000 RPM (tiers 2-3), 2000 RPM (tiers 4-5). Programmatic Tool Calling (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling) lets the model emit JavaScript that runs in an isolated V8 runtime and orchestrates tools, which 'can reduce the amount of intermediate tool output added to model context'; no numeric limits on tools, result size or runtime are published, and a running program cannot itself invoke tool search. ChatGPT-product MCP (https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461-developer-mode-apps-and-full-mcp-connectors-in-chatgpt-beta): full MCP with write actions is in beta for Business/Enterprise/Edu; Pro is read/fetch only; multiple first- and third-party apps may be invoked in one prompt with no published app-count cap. Per-model RPM/TPM rate limits apply and are listed on each model page. Programmatic Tool Calling is listed as supported on this model's page.

strict_function_schema.notes: Structured Outputs strict mode applies to function/tool parameters: additionalProperties:false everywhere, all properties required, root may not be anyOf, and a documented list of unsupported keywords. See tool_schema_limits_notes for the unresolved 100-vs-5,000 property-count conflict.

skills_loading_model.notes: Progressive disclosure, not always-on injection: a skill is 'a versioned bundle of files plus a SKILL.md manifest', and the platform adds only each skill's name, description and path to prompt context; the model reads the full SKILL.md only when it decides to invoke the skill.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: Two-stage cost. Stage 1 (always paid, per request): the name + description + path stub for every attached skill. Stage 2 (paid only on invocation): the full SKILL.md body, and any bundled files the model reads. Docs are explicit that 'Skill instructions are user prompt input (not system prompt input), so they're handled with the same priority as other user-provided instructions' — which also means they are ordinary input tokens. Ingest caps documented 2026-08-19: 50 MB max zip upload, 500 max files per skill version, 25 MB max uncompressed file. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-skills.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: The Responses API prepends hidden scaffolding for every enabled surface (MCP server tool lists, skill stubs, hosted-tool definitions). OpenAI does not publish its token size. Measure it empirically by POSTing the same payload with and without each tool to /v1/responses/input_tokens (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/token-counting) and differencing.

prompt_caching.notes: Automatic caching from the 1,024-token minimum. gpt-5.4 is listed under Extended Prompt Cache Retention (up to 24h) in addition to the short in-memory tier; cached input bills at 0.1x, and there is no 1.25x cache-write surcharge (that starts with GPT-5.6). Tool definitions, tool ordering and structured-output schemas are part of the cached prefix.

memory_feature.notes: No model-side persistent memory in the API. The agents guide frames state as application-managed — SDK sessions, the Conversations API, manual history, or resumable run state. ChatGPT's 'Memory' and Codex's memories are product features, not this model's API surface.

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Unchanged. Standard processing under 272K input tokens; regional data-residency processing adds a 10% uplift.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Image input billed as input tokens via 32x32 patch counting (auto == high on this model, i.e. a 2,500-patch ceiling by default). Audio not supported.

models.notes: SUPERSEDED but still GA. reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: reasoning_effort: none (default), low, medium, high, xhigh. Reasoning tokens bill as output.

Previous entry cited include=['usage'] round-trips instead.

image_token_rule.value: Patch-based (32x32 pixel patches), same GPT-5.x scheme as gpt-5.4: detail low / high / original / auto, up to 2,500 patches at high and 10,000 at original, token cost = patch count x a model-specific multiplier. Image input only.

MCP tool-call rate limits: 200 RPM (tier 1), 1000 RPM (tiers 2-3), 2000 RPM (tiers 4-5). Programmatic Tool Calling (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling) lets the model emit JavaScript that runs in an isolated V8 runtime and orchestrates tools, which 'can reduce the amount of intermediate tool output added to model context'; no numeric limits on tools, result size or runtime are published, and a running program cannot itself invoke tool search. ChatGPT-product MCP (https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461-developer-mode-apps-and-full-mcp-connectors-in-chatgpt-beta): full MCP with write actions is in beta for Business/Enterprise/Edu; Pro is read/fetch only; multiple first- and third-party apps may be invoked in one prompt with no published app-count cap. Per-model RPM/TPM rate limits apply and are listed on each model page. Programmatic Tool Calling is not listed on this model's feature table; verify before use.

strict_function_schema.notes: Structured Outputs strict mode applies to function/tool parameters: additionalProperties:false everywhere, all properties required, root may not be anyOf, and a documented list of unsupported keywords. See tool_schema_limits_notes for the unresolved 100-vs-5,000 property-count conflict.

skills_loading_model.notes: Progressive disclosure, not always-on injection: a skill is 'a versioned bundle of files plus a SKILL.md manifest', and the platform adds only each skill's name, description and path to prompt context; the model reads the full SKILL.md only when it decides to invoke the skill.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: Two-stage cost. Stage 1 (always paid, per request): the name + description + path stub for every attached skill. Stage 2 (paid only on invocation): the full SKILL.md body, and any bundled files the model reads. Docs are explicit that 'Skill instructions are user prompt input (not system prompt input), so they're handled with the same priority as other user-provided instructions' — which also means they are ordinary input tokens. Ingest caps documented 2026-08-19: 50 MB max zip upload, 500 max files per skill version, 25 MB max uncompressed file. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-skills.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: The Responses API prepends hidden scaffolding for every enabled surface (MCP server tool lists, skill stubs, hosted-tool definitions). OpenAI does not publish its token size. Measure it empirically by POSTing the same payload with and without each tool to /v1/responses/input_tokens (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/token-counting) and differencing.

prompt_caching.notes: Automatic caching from the 1,024-token minimum; cached input bills at 0.1x ($0.075/1M). Confidence caveat: the prompt-caching guide's Extended Prompt Cache Retention list names gpt-5.5, gpt-5.5-pro, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.2, gpt-5.1 variants, gpt-5 and gpt-4.1 but does NOT name gpt-5.4-mini, so 24h retention on this model is not confirmed — the standard short in-memory tier should be assumed. Previous entry asserted 24h; corrected 2026-08-19.

memory_feature.notes: No model-side persistent memory in the API. The agents guide frames state as application-managed — SDK sessions, the Conversations API, manual history, or resumable run state. ChatGPT's 'Memory' and Codex's memories are product features, not this model's API surface.

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Unchanged. Regional data-residency processing adds a 10% uplift.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Image input billed as input tokens via the GPT-5.x 32x32 patch scheme. Audio not supported.
